---
title: Resolver & Modes
description: How Figma modes become DTCG Resolver contexts for theming.
---

Figma collections can have multiple modes (Light/Dark, Compact/Comfortable, etc.). DTCG Resolver expresses which token file applies under each context.

## Generated file

`tokens/tokens.resolver.json` lists modifier axes and defaults:

```json
{
  "name": "Figma Variables",
  "modifiers": {
    "semantic": {
      "contexts": {
        "light": { "groups": ["semantic"] },
        "dark": { "groups": ["semantic.dark"] }
      },
      "default": "light"
    }
  }
}
```

Exact shape depends on your Figma file structure.

## Runtime switching

**CSS:** theme blocks use `[data-semantic="dark"]` (or similar) selectors generated in `tokens.css`.

**React:** `useTheme().setContext('semantic', 'dark')` updates active contexts and re-resolves `useToken` values.

**MCP:** pass contexts to `resolve_context`:

```json
{ "contexts": { "semantic": "dark" } }
```

## Naming

Collection names are slugified to axis keys. Mode names become context ids (`Light` → `light`).

If something looks wrong after build, open `tokens.resolver.json` first. It is the source of truth for how modes connect.
